title: lore export help and manifest advertise schema 1.0 and ship an example that fails; the exporter writes 1.1
description:
REPRODUCED 2026-09-15 against the INSTALLED 0.7.0 binary (/Users/jdnewhouse/.nvm/versions/node/v24.20.0/bin/lore, `lore --version` -> 0.7.0), not against a dev checkout. Reported by an external user on the mbpm2 project, relayed via opum-agent; reproduced here before filing rather than taken on report.

WHAT THE TOOL ADVERTISES:

  $ lore export --help
    Flags:
      --schema-version <value>  Projection schema version (currently 1.0)
    Examples:
      lore export
      lore export --schema-version 1.0

WHAT THE ADVERTISED EXAMPLE DOES:

  $ lore export --schema-version 1.0
  error: unsupported projection schema version "1.0"
  hint: this lore supports 1.1
  exit 2

  $ lore export --schema-version 1.1   -> exit 0
  $ lore export                         -> exit 0

So the shipped help does not merely carry a stale number: IT SHIPS AN EXAMPLE THAT CANNOT WORK. A user copying the documented invocation gets a usage error. Exit 2 is the correct semantic code for that usage error, so the runtime behaviour is right and the defect is entirely in the advertised text.

ROOT CAUSE, LOCATED:

  src/core/projection.ts:17   export const PROJECTION_SCHEMA_VERSION = "1.1"   <- the truth
  src/core/manifest.ts:770    summary: "Projection schema version (currently 1.0)"   <- literal
  src/core/manifest.ts:776    examples: [..., "lore export --schema-version 1.0"]    <- literal
  src/commands/export.ts:1    stale module doc comment naming 1.0

The constant EXISTS and the code that matters already uses it -- export.ts:72 interpolates it into the usage hint, ladybug-source.ts:727 interpolates it into a remedy string. Only the manifest, which is what `--help` and `lore manifest` render, hardcodes the number.

THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE SHAPE IN THIS REPOSITORY, and the first two are already fixed, which is what makes the remedy obvious rather than a judgement call:
  LCLI-494  every projection record claimed `backlog-json/1` regardless of the
            backend that produced it -> fixed by putting sourceAdapterVersion on
            the TrackerAdapter interface.
  LCLI-503  three status-flow throws named `backlog/config.yml` while the flow came
            from the polymorphic adapter -> fixed by putting statusFlowHints on the
            same interface.
  THIS      the manifest names 1.0 while the exporter writes PROJECTION_SCHEMA_VERSION.

The reporter's proposed fix is the same move and should be adopted as proposed: generate the help summary and the examples FROM the constant, and TEST the examples. A copy that is derived cannot drift; a copy that is maintained will.

THE NUANCE A NAIVE FIX WOULD DESTROY, and it is the reason this is not a one-line substitution. src/core/projection.ts:37 is

  READABLE_PROJECTION_SCHEMA_VERSIONS = ["1.0", PROJECTION_SCHEMA_VERSION]

with the comment "Every export schema lore can READ, newest last. Writing is always PROJECTION_SCHEMA_VERSION". So 1.0 is NOT a dead number -- lore still reads it, and only writing is pinned to 1.1. `--schema-version` is a WRITE selector, which is why 1.0 is rejected there and why the help was not absurd when written. Substituting 1.1 for 1.0 in both places would be correct and would silently discard the read/write distinction. The generated summary should say which of the two it means.

ALSO WORTH FIXING WHILE THERE: the error's "this lore supports 1.1" is true of writing and incomplete overall, since lore reads 1.0 too. A reader holding a 1.0 projection is told their version is unsupported when it is in fact still readable.

WHAT THE SAME REPORTER CONFIRMED WORKING, recorded because a validation report's positive half usually goes unrecorded and this one bears on a known defect: expanded 111-test suite with zero skips and real CLI integration tests; log preservation and `sync --fail-on-drop`, INCLUDING refusal BEFORE documentation or tracker changes (the ordering property a weaker implementation gets wrong); bounded Lore context with explicit omissions and exact reads; typed proof relations, dependency traversal, version-drift warnings, claim-metadata preservation. Given LCLI-474's log-truncation history, independent external confirmation of log preservation and fail-on-drop under a real integration suite is stronger evidence than any first-party note.

Source report: results/analysis/proof-graph-pilot-20260913/build-validation/lore-0.7.0-quest-0.7.1-20260915/validation-report.md (mbpm2 project; not read by this session -- the defect above was reproduced independently from the description).

SCOPE: rides along with a 0.7.1 rather than justifying one, same category as LCLI-503. Does not displace LCLI-502/510/507.
